title: Recover exact interrupted record transactions
description: Resolve an explicitly selected supported interrupted publication by completing its prepared candidate or restoring its verified before-state. Recovery preserves the supplied engineering decisions exactly and never reconstructs them by replaying operations against new state.
inputs: Explicit change, transaction and expected-recovery identity with requested restore or complete action.
Supported private journal, exact verified before/candidate snapshots, observed targets, and declared read-set identities.
outputs: Verified restored or completed storage result, or an explicit safe recovery stop.
Retained recoverability for another interrupted attempt, with refreshed recovery identity when available.
behavior: Validate journal/version, snapshots, containment and explicit expected recovery identity before mutation; reject unsupported retired or mixed recovery selectors.
At observed checks, require each target to match recorded before or candidate bytes/absence; never overwrite a third state.
Complete only the exact prepared candidate with current declared read basis; restore only verified before content while leaving external read subjects untouched.
Protect acknowledged committed success from rollback; restoration of initial creation removes only transaction-created content and empty created directories.
Keep recovery repeatable after interruption and clean private snapshots only after verified terminal recovery; those snapshots are mechanical recovery state rather than engineering evidence.

failure_behavior.condition: Evidence is missing, corrupt, tampered, incompatible, or a target has an unknown third state.
failure_behavior.outcome: Stop without guessed repair or foreign-content overwrite, preserving available recovery context.

failure_behavior.condition: Completion basis drifts or recovery is interrupted again.
failure_behavior.outcome: Report the corresponding safe stop/recovery-required state; do not silently choose restoration or synthesize a new decision.
